test_title: PYST 54: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 21 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Why was Acko General Insurance fined ₹1 crore by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) in May 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Payments to an unregistered intermediary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** imposed a significant monetary penalty of **₹1 crore** on **Acko General Insurance** in **May 2025**.
 
• The penalty was levied following a regulatory investigation that uncovered **violations related to payments made to an unregistered intermediary**. According to **IRDAI** regulations, insurance companies are prohibited from transacting or paying commissions to entities that do not hold a valid license to act as an insurance intermediary.
 
• Investigations revealed that the company had entered into arrangements where payouts were channeled to entities that were not authorized under the **IRDAI (Registration of Insurance Marketing Firms) Regulations** or the **Insurance Act, 1938**.
 
• The regulatory body observed that such practices bypass the transparent commission structures mandated for the industry and can lead to higher costs for policyholders. ***Hence, the primary reason for the fine was payments to an unregistered intermediary.***
 
• This enforcement action is part of **IRDAI's** broader mandate to maintain market discipline and ensure that all stakeholders in the insurance distribution chain are properly regulated and accountable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **IRDAI (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India):**
 
 
• It is a statutory body formed under the **IRDA Act, 1999**. It serves as the apex regulatory authority for the insurance sector in **India**.
 
• Headquartered in **Hyderabad**, its primary objectives include protecting the interests of policyholders and regulating, promoting, and ensuring the orderly growth of the insurance industry.
 
 
 
• **Acko General Insurance:**
 
 
• Founded in **2016** by **Varun Dua**, it is a prominent **Insurtech** company in **India** that follows a direct-to-consumer model.
 
• The company specializes in **digital-first** insurance products, including motor, health, and electronics insurance, often leveraging data and technology to offer competitive premiums.
 
 
 
• **Insurance Intermediaries:**
 
 
• These include agents, brokers, corporate agents, and web aggregators who act as a bridge between the insurance company and the customer.
 
• Under **Section 42** of the **Insurance Act, 1938**, no person can act as an intermediary or receive remuneration for procuring insurance business unless they are registered with the **IRDAI**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Insurance Act, 1938:** This is the cornerstone legislation for insurance in **India**. **Section 40** of this Act specifically prohibits the payment of any commission or brokerage to any person for soliciting or procuring insurance business in **India**, unless that person is an authorized agent or intermediary.
 
• **Regulatory Compliance:** **IRDAI** conducts periodic inspections and **audits** of insurance firms. Non-compliance with the **Expenses of Management (EoM)** limits or unauthorized payouts often results in stiff penalties, as seen in the **2025** ruling against **Acko**.
 
• **Solvency Ratio:** While not the reason for this specific fine, **IRDAI** mandates a minimum **solvency ratio** of **1.5 (150%)** for all insurers to ensure they have sufficient capital to settle claims even during financial stress.
 
• **Impact of Penalties:** Fines of this nature serve as a deterrent to other players in the **Insurtech** and traditional insurance space, emphasizing that digital innovation must go hand-in-hand with strict **regulatory compliance**.
